summary: A 1960 14x14 flat-top cab on a site first developed in 1923, in Oregon's Willamette National Forest; open to hikers, volunteer-maintained, and not staffed.

facts.design: 14 x 14 ft R-6 flat-top cab on a short 4 ft wooden base (1960); site first developed in 1923 with a D-6 cupola cabin

visit.trail_note: About 1 mile, rated moderate. The final approach crosses a rock face with a handrail. No water or restroom.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Both dates are kept. The 1923 cupola was the first structure on the site; the 1960 R-6 cab is the one standing, per the register and the Forest Service.

Firelookout.com says abandoned for many years; the Forest Service says it has volunteer maintenance and is in very good condition; Oregon Hikers says restored in 2004. The Forest Service is the current official source, so the story leans on it and reports the older description.
Register 3,988 ft; Forest Service 4,243 ft. Both are reported; neither source says how its figure was measured.

notes_for_editor: Current access and staffing rest on the Forest Service page (undated in our copy; treated as 2026). The 2004 restoration rests only on Oregon Hikers, a volunteer-edited wiki; the 2004 scanned report cited in the brief (firelookout.org cr-or-2004.pdf) has no text layer and could not be machine-checked, so it is not used. The brief's 2004 rental-program claim comes from that same PDF and is omitted; no source read mentions a rental program. Firelookout.com also gives elevation 4255 ft; search snippets (not read as pages) also show 4,236 ft (Oregon Hikers) and 4243 ft (Outerspatial). The story reports only the register and Forest Service figures. The Bedrock Fire is named with no date (none found in sources read), so the story gives no year. The brief record's elevation_m 1215.5 matches the register. The brief record had only the 1960 build; the 1923 cupola and 1967 standby events are added from the register.
